chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding the solemn oath (Ila'): When a man takes an oath that he will not approach his wife, nor touch her, nor join his head with her head, he is in a period of grace as long as four months do not pass. When four months have passed, he is paused (given a choice): either he fulfills (the oath by returning), so he touches her, or he is determined upon divorce, so he separates from her until she menstruates and becomes pure from her menstruation, then he divorces her with one divorce before he sleeps with her, with the testimony of two just witnesses. Then he is more rightful in reverting to her as long as the three pure periods (Quroo') do not pass.

key_terms.الْإِيلَاءِ: Solemn oath of abstention from wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and procedure for Ila' (solemn oath of abstention) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the procedural mechanics of Ila', emphasizing the husband's four-month grace period before being compelled to choose between resuming intimacy or initiating divorce. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that the final divorce occurs after one menstrual cycle, preserving the husband's right of revocation (Raj'ah) during the three subsequent pure periods, a structure designed to balance marital stability with the resolution of prolonged abstention.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Bureyd Bin Muawiya who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying regarding the solemn oath when the man oaths that he would not approach his wife and will not touch her, nor gather his head and her head, so he is in a leeway for as long as four months do not pass by. So when four months pass by, he pauses. So either he fulfils, so he touches her, and if he is determined upon the divorce, so he separates from her until she menstruates and is pure from her menstruation, divorces her with one divorce before he sleeps with her, with two just witnesses. Then he is more rightful with reverting back to her for as long as three Quroos (pure periods) do not pass by her’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Burayd ibn Mu‘awiyah who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, state this Hadith.

‘If a man swears not to go to bed with his wife, not to touch her and not to place his head next to her head, he then has the choice before passing of four months. When four months pass he then must be taken in custody to reach a settlement and go to bed with her, or decide to divorce, thus, he must leave her until she experiences Hayd (menses) and becomes clean from Hayd (menses), then divorce her once before going to bed with her and in the presence of two just witnesses. Thereafter he has the right to go back to her until her passing three cycles of Hayd (menses)-free periods.”’
